title: The specified strict quotient augmentation of a complete object is invertible
statement: Fix distinct primes p,l and a finite extension E/Q_l. Let W be a scheme and L:SiteLimitData l E W a normalized total derived inverse-limit model [def-pur-completed-pushforward-models]. Let K be derived complete [def-weil-derived-complete] and r:Q(P) isomorphic to K for a flat-term K-flat completed-module complex P. Let C be a complex of strict towers and e:C.asFunctor isomorphic to the actual unrestrictedIntegralComplexTower(P) [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. If a:P to lim(C) is a chain map satisfying IsReductionAugmentation, then r inverse followed by Q(a) and L.limit.unit at C is invertible. This asserts invertibility of this normalized map itself, not existence of an unspecified isomorphism between its endpoints.

proof.text: Use a witness of the published Roos-triangle completeness condition. Its triangle and the explicit strict quotient Roos triangle have the same last two vertices and one-minus-shift map; rotation gives an isomorphism of their first vertices. The quotient Roos object is locally derived complete by the principal-cone quotient comparison and the local completion criterion. Transport local completeness to K. This is the first implication of the recorded Roos/intrinsic equivalence, specialized without its unused adic-datum parameter.

proof.text: Apply the principal scalar-cone local criterion to the given K-flat representative P and r. The criterion makes its specified principal-cone unit invertible. Compose with the unit-preserving principal-cone/quotient Roos comparison to obtain invertibility of r.inv followed by Q of the actual quotient Roos unit. No flat-term hypothesis beyond the unchanged theorem signature is required here.

proof.text: Construct the canonical isomorphism between the termwise ordinary limit and the limit in the category of complexes by their limit cones. Compare the strict Roos derivation with source.limit by uniqueness of total right derived functors, retaining its ordinary-limit unit equation. The sectionwise formula ha identifies the transported augmentation with the quotient units at every level. Naturality of the zero-homotopy mapping-cocone lift gives equality of the entire specified chain maps after the strict tower isomorphism e, including their zero second coordinates. Localization and composition with these comparison isomorphisms prove invertibility of the requested map itself.

theorem reductionAugmentation_isIso (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hlp : l ≠ p)
    (W : Scheme.{t}) (source : SiteLimitData l E W)
    (K : DerivedCategory (Mod W (R l E W)))
    (P : CochainComplex (Mod W (R l E W)) ℤ)
    (hP : CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients
      (R := completedIntegralCommRingSheafUnrestricted l E W) P)
    (hflat : ∀ i : ℤ, @SheafOfModules.IsFlatOnSite W.ProEt inferInstance (ProEt.topology W)
      inferInstance (integralCoefficientAbLocallyBijective.{t, u} W)
      (integralCoefficientAbSheafify.{t, u} W).isRightAdjoint
      (completedIntegralCommRingSheafUnrestricted l E W) (P.X i))
    (r : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ≅ K)
    (C : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Mod W (R l E W)) ℤ)
    (e : C.asFunctor ≅ unrestrictedIntegralComplexTower l E W P)
    (a : P ⟶ ((ordinaryTowerLimit l E W).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj C)
    (ha : IsReductionAugmentation l E W P C e a)
    (hK : IsDerivedCompleteUnrestricted l E W K) :
    IsIso (r.inv ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map a ≫ source.limit.unit.app C)
